House Bill 314 (COMMITTEE SUBSTITUTE) By: Representatives LaHood of the 175th, Powell of the 33rd, Jasperse of the 11th, Cannon of the 172nd, and Sharper of the 177th
A BILL TO BE ENTITLED AN ACT
To amend Chapter 5 of Title 43 of … recognition, evaluation, management, disposition, rehabilitation, and treatment. Nothing in this Code section shall be construed to require licensure of elementary or secondary school teachers, coaches, or authorized volunteers who do not hold themselves out to the public as athletic trainers. Athletic trainers who perform dry needling procedures are required to demonstrate proof of graduation from a program of study that included dry needling instruction consisting of a minimum of 50 hours and a competency assessment of achievement in its curriculum. Online study for dry needling instruction will not be accepted as a demonstration of competence and training. (3) 'Board' means the Georgia Board of Athletic Trainers."
SECTION 2. Said chapter is further amended by revising Code Section 43-5-6, relating to general powers and duties of the Georgia Board for Athletic Trainers, as follows: "43-5-6. (a) The … performance of its duties. (b) The board shall prescribe application forms for license applications. (c) The board shall establish guidelines for athletic trainers in the state and prepare and conduct an approve a certification examination for applicants for a license. (d) The board shall adopt an official seal and the form of a license certificate of suitable design."
SECTION 3. Said chapter is further amended by revising Code Section 43-5-7, relating to license requirement for persons engaged as athletic … (a) An applicant for an athletic trainer's license must have met the athletic training curriculum requirements of a college or university approved shall be a graduate of an accredited educational program that prepares athletic trainers recognized by the board and give proof of graduation or shall submit, in a manner prescribed by the board, equivalent educational credentials as approved by the board. (b) The board shall be authorized to grant a license, without examination, to any qualified athletic trainer holding a license in another state if such other state recognizes licensees of this state in the same manner. (c) The board may … for licensure, notwithstanding the requirement for proof of graduation in subsection (a) of this Code section, so long as the license remains current."
SECTION 5. All laws and parts of laws in conflict with this Act are repealed.
